Verdict: REVISE — local proof-text correction only; no substantive geometric counterexampleYour correction to my earlier charge objection is valid. I had incorrectly counted the two R bar-end supports as lying inside the endpoint-tile footprint. Under the supplied constructor and the chart parity, those supports lie in the adjacent physical tile columns outside the entire R endpoint footprint.For the supplied source constructor:
$$R:\quad 71/45/18\longmapsto 71+18-2\cdot45=-1,$$
and for the sharp witness,
$$R_{\mathrm{sharp}}:\quad 65/41/16
\longmapsto 65+16-2\cdot41=-1.$$
The retained mass assertions are therefore correct. My previous  $+2$  support count was an error.The repaired earlier-original partition also resolves my prior wording objection. I find no remaining counterexample to the main gain formula, the four E-frontier phases, the  $\chi$  triple-owner correction, the nonstacking inequality, or the automatic disjoint-footprint argument.I nevertheless return REVISE, because one support-classification sentence in the revised general T-count proof is still false even though its final numerical count is correct.1. Correct R charge countFor
$$R=U(L,10,f),\qquad
\operatorname{chart}(r,c)=(a_i-11+r,C_i+1-c),$$
the constructor offset is
$$(a_i-11,C_i+1),$$
which is even/even.The supplied count is
$$\begin{aligned}
\#\operatorname{matching}(R)
 &=L+4+\frac f2,\\
\#\operatorname{endpointTiles}(R)
 &=\frac L2+5+\frac f2,\\
\#\operatorname{originalSupportsInside}(R)
 &=5+\frac f2.
\end{aligned}$$
The last count decomposes as follows:the two bar-end supports  $(0,0)$  and  $(0,L+1)$  are outside the entire endpoint-tile footprint;the depth-ten near lateral supports at intrinsic rows  $3,5,7,9$  contribute  $4$ ;the far lateral supports at rows  $3,5,\ldots,f-1$  contribute  $f/2-1$ ;the two axial terminal supports contribute  $2$ .Thus
$$\#\operatorname{originalSupportsInside}(R)
=
4+\left(\frac f2-1\right)+2
=
5+\frac f2.$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
c(R)
&=
\left(L+4+\frac f2\right)
+\left(5+\frac f2\right)
-2\left(\frac L2+5+\frac f2\right)\\
&=-1.
\end{aligned}$$
So  $R$  contributes one unit of negative mass, exactly as the original theorem and verifier assert.The concrete values supplied in the revised note are consistent:
$$R_{\mathrm{triple}}:\quad
71+18-90=-1,$$
and
$$R_{\mathrm{sharp}}:\quad
65+16-82=-1.$$
The old charge objection is withdrawn.2. The T charge formula is numerically correct, but its support classification is notFor
$$T=U(M,4,g),\qquad
\operatorname{chart}(r,c)=(a_i-8+r,s_i+1-c),$$
the constructor offset is odd/odd. The numerical counts are
$$\begin{aligned}
\#\operatorname{matching}(T)
 &=M+1+\frac g2,\\
\#\operatorname{endpointTiles}(T)
 &=M+2+\frac g2,\\
\#\operatorname{originalSupportsInside}(T)
 &=4+\frac g2.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
c(T)
&=
\left(M+1+\frac g2\right)
+\left(4+\frac g2\right)
-2\left(M+2+\frac g2\right)\\
&=1-M.
\end{aligned}$$
That agrees with the original mass ledger.However, the explanatory sentence in SECONDARY_TEN_BOTH_FAR_CHARGE_SEPARATION.md says:“The near and far lateral supports contribute  $1$  and  $g/2-1$ , and both axial supports are inside.”That support-location classification is not correct for the supplied affine constructor.The correct T support partition is:the two bar-end supports are inside;the near lateral supports at the even intrinsic rows  $2,4$  contribute  $2$ ;the far lateral supports at even rows  $2,4,\ldots,g$  contribute  $g/2$ ;both axial terminal supports at intrinsic rows  $5$  and  $g+1$  are outside the endpoint-tile footprint.Therefore the correct decomposition is
$$\#\operatorname{originalSupportsInside}(T)
=
2+2+\frac g2
=
4+\frac g2.$$
The total count and charge are unchanged, but the proof should state this actual partition. This is a local correction, not a failure of the charge formula or of the gain theorem.For the supplied example  $M=28,g=24$ ,
$$41+16-2\cdot42=-27=1-M,$$
as claimed.3. The source-level mass ledger is now correctWith the corrected R and T counts,
$$c(R)=-1,\qquad c(T)=1-M.$$
Thus a selected pair contributes negative mass
$$1+(M-1)=M$$
and no positive-owner count. Consequently the source contribution in the one-pair ledger is exactly
$$(1-d)+(M-1-\delta)=M-d-\delta.$$
The previous proposed changes to the mass assertions are therefore unnecessary. The original assertions should be retained.This correction does not change:the E-frontier deduction  $d$ ;the T-frontier deduction  $\delta$ ;the mutual contribution  $-2\epsilon$ ;the triple-owner contribution  $+2\chi$ ;the final pair identity.4. The repaired earlier-original separation is sufficientThe revised E-frontier note now partitions earlier originals into:the nine base originals  $B_j$ ;the repair  $P_j$ ;the west rotor  $Z_j$ ;the south  $U$ -owner  $X_j$ ;the root  $K$ .That repair resolves the prior objection.For  $j<i$ ,
$$\min\operatorname{col}(B_j)\ge s_j+2
\ge s_{i-1}+2
=C_i+1.$$
Every R endpoint has column at most  $C_i$ . Since  $C_i$  is odd and  $C_i+1$  is even, the two sets lie in adjacent physical tile columns and cannot share a tile.The root has the same right-side column separation.The earlier  $P_j,Z_j,X_j$  owners need the row argument instead. Their maximum rows are bounded by
$$a_j+2\le a_i-16,$$
whereas R starts at row  $a_i-11$ . Since the physical tile rows are formed from consecutive row pairs, those earlier endpoints lie strictly above every R endpoint tile row.This is an exhaustive partition, and it handles arbitrarily deep earlier base stems because the base family is separated by columns rather than by a depth cutoff. I find no remaining gap in that repaired dependency.5. The new E-frontier table remains valid for arbitrary  $f$ The four frontier phases and their deductions remain correct:
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c}
F & \text{legal terminal condition} & d\\ \hline
s_k-4 & b\le a_k-3 & 0\\
s_k-2 & b\le a_k-3 & 1\text{ only if }b=a_k-3\\
s_k & b\le a_k-5 & 2\text{ if }b\in\{a_k-7,a_k-5\}\\
s_k+2\le F\le s_{k-1}-6
 & b\le a_k-9
 & 1\text{ only if }b=a_k-9.
\end{array}$$
The support exclusions at the phase boundaries are also consistent: $F=s_k-4$ : the apparent  $R/X_k$  vertical contact is excluded in both directions by the two axial supports; $F=s_k-2$ : the surviving receipt is one full tile and three events; $F=s_k$ : the  $P_k$ -far receipt has  $h$  full tiles and  $2h+2$  events, giving signed value  $-2$ ; $F\ge s_k+2$ : the terminal case has exactly one surviving  $P_k\to R$  event.The arbitrary far depth  $f$  introduces no further old contact because the legal terminal bounds stop the continuous stem above the first later-block body. The same remains true for arbitrary  $g$  under the accepted left-chain exterior theorem.6. The nonstacking inequality and triple correction remain validFor  $q\ge2$ ,
$$\epsilon=0.$$
For  $q=0$  and  $d>0$ , the coupled E/T frontier cases force
$$y<b.$$
Hence  $\epsilon=0$  whenever  $d>0$ , and therefore
$$d+2\epsilon\le2.$$
The  $\chi$  term is also correct. In the only possible triple-owner case,
$$F=s_k-4,\qquad b=a_k-3,\qquad y\ge a_k-2.$$
The additional full tile contains R, T, and  $X_k$ . It is absent from both separate receipts and contributes  $+2$ . The possible  $X_k\to T$  event is already contained in the T-frontier receipt, while the reverse direction is excluded by T’s immutable support. No further event is missing.Thus
$$\Delta\Phi_i
=
M_i-d_i-\delta_i-2\epsilon_i+2\chi_i$$
still holds exactly.7. Automatic selected-pair footprint separation remains validFor each pair,
$$F_j=s_j-M_j-q_j,\qquad
C_j=s_j+w_j+13,$$
with  $F_j$  even and  $C_j$  odd. The aligned R bar contains an endpoint in every integer column of  $[F_j,C_j]$ , and the whole T footprint lies inside the same tile-column envelope.If  $i<j$ , all nonfar endpoints of pair  $i$  end above the first R-bar row  $a_j-11$  of pair  $j$ . If an earlier R or T far stem shared a physical tile column with pair  $j$ , its column  $x$  would satisfy
$$F_j\le x\le C_j.$$
If its terminal reached  $a_j-11$ , it would collide with the R-bar endpoint at
$$(a_j-11,x).$$
Endpoint-disjointness therefore forces its terminal strictly above that row. The parity of the two possible terminals then gives strict physical tile-row separation.Hence pair endpoint-tile footprints are disjoint. Every new full tile and every new directed event contains a new endpoint, so the new full-tile and owner-labelled event sets are disjoint unions of the per-pair sets. Immutable source supports prevent any insertion-order or support-reclassification problem.Final decisionREVISE.The main theorem is mathematically supported after the corrected R charge count and the repaired exhaustive earlier-original separation. I found no substantive counterexample to:the arbitrary- $f/g$  frontier table;the exact pair gain; $d+2\epsilon\le2$ ;the  $\chi$  triple-owner correction;automatic disjoint full pair footprints;exact set-level nonreuse.The required remaining repair is precise and local:
$$\boxed{
\text{For }T,\ 
\text{near lateral inside}=2,\ 
\text{far lateral inside}=g/2,\ 
\text{both axial supports outside}.
}$$
This still gives
$$\operatorname{originalSupportsInside}(T)=4+\frac g2,
\qquad
c(T)=1-M.$$
After correcting that support-classification sentence, I would treat the selected-union theorem as ACCEPT, conditional on the already stated endpoint-disjointness hypotheses and the accepted short-pair/left-chain dependencies. No complete-extension, global  $5/6$ , catalogue-exhaustion, or later sharpness claim is implied.
